entries.title: The logarithmic boundary profile must stay positive at the initial scale
entries.locator: arXiv:2204.12410v2, Lemma 2.5 and equations (12)–(13), printed p.8 / PDF index7, extracted lines648–681; equation (18), printed p.10 / PDF index9, lines942–969. Versioned HTML and extracted PDF text agree. No journal-formula or visual-PDF comparison.
entries.claim: The lemma includes every positive integer radius n and uses f(n,1)=log(n)/n in its boundary-functional upper bound.
entries.problem: At n=1 this factor is zero. For d>=2, J(z)=||z||_infinity^(-d-1) and beta>0, the boundary functional of Lambda_1 is positive: its term with inside endpoint0 and outside endpoint2e_1 is q_beta(2e_1)>0. The internal root connection has probability one. Thus the displayed upper bound cannot hold at that radius.
entries.correction: Use f_1(n)=log(en)/n for all n>=1, as in31X5 andVVB0, or retain log(n)/n and require n>=2. PTM2 proves the underlying crossing-profile bound, and the harmonic-sum comparison then holds at every admitted radius. The exponent conclusions are unchanged.
entries.leanImpact: Specify n>=1, prove summability and the displacement crossing count before interchanging sums, and use a positive logarithmic profile before taking a reciprocal. Critical flux requires a finite critical intensity. This is a written local repair, with no compiled association or author confirmation.

resolution.summary: Replace log(n) by log(en), or start the estimate at n=2.
resolution.impact: Only the initial scale changes; the exponent conclusions are retained.
